messages:
morgan: quick heads-up — during the private VPC roll we hit a KMS decryption failure and the service fell back to a cached plaintext key. unsure how the cache was allowed to be used. need triage. :rotating_light:
ara: which cluster/region and timestamps? can you paste the error lines?
morgan: cluster=priv-eu-1, deploy=inference-gateway, ~2026-03-21T09:12Z. logs: ```ERROR: KMS decrypt timed out (500ms). falling back to local cache for key_id=customer-kms/rdw-key-82
WARN: using cached plaintext key from in-memory keystore, ttl=12h```
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 opened (severity=P2). Assigned to eng-security. See runbook: https://go/runbooks/priv-kms-fallback
sam: oof. immediate steps: 1) remove cached key from the pod(s), 2) apply netpol to block egress to any KMS fallback endpoints, 3) start key rotation. we should also snapshot audit logs.
devon: +1. can you `kubectl -n inference exec` into the gateway and clear `/var/run/keystore/*`? also confirm whether the keystore is node-local or sidecar-managed — that affects blast radius.
morgan: keystore is sidecar-managed (keystore-sidecar:v2). I can exec and clear, but want to ensure we don't break live traffic without a fallback route.
lex: heads-up — I merged an RBAC tweak last week that relaxed `keystore:read` for the monitoring-sa to allow ephemeral read during startup (PR #4782). can we check if that change allowed unintended reads that populated the cache? PR: https://git.internal/r/4782
ara: if RBAC allowed an unauthenticated path that could write the cache, it's bad. but the log shows decrypt timeout then fallback — seems like network/e2e to KMS timed out. need to know why KMS call timed out. is this customer KMS behind a private gateway?
morgan: customer KMS is reachable via a NATless proxy in the VPC — our egress rule to that proxy uses conntrack and an AWS ALB. there was a small restart of the proxy at 09:10Z per infra-alerts.
devon: that aligns — proxy restart -> KMS timeouts -> fallback to cache. mitigation path: 1) revoke the cached key instances 2) temporarily route KMS calls to fallback alternate endpoint (kms-replica), 3) tighten netpol so only gateway -> proxy allowed.
sam: for step 1: command to clear cache on all replicas: ```kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-gateway -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n inference exec {} -- rm -f /var/run/keystore/*.key && kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-gateway```
ara: also we need to validate audit logging: do we have KMS decrypt attempts forwarded to SIEM? if not, enable immediate forward and capture 1h retention for forensic.
lex: I can revert the RBAC change quickly if we think it contributed. but from the flow it sounds more like proxy availability. still revert to be safe, patch added auth check to the keystore API.
sec-bot: Action checklist updated on INC-2026-0423: [clear-cache] @morgan, [apply-netpol] @devon, [rotate-keys] @sam, [revert-rbac-pr] @lex, [collect-audit] @ara. ETA 60m.
morgan: starting cache purge now, will report when done.
morgan: cache purge done on 3/3 replicas, restarting gateway. no errors on restart.
devon: applying restrictive netpol that denies all egress except to kms-proxy svc. snippet: ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms-proxy
  namespace: inference
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference-gateway
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443```
sam: started key rotation with the customer KMS admin. rotating primary key and scheduling rollout. once rotated, force service tokens to refresh.
ara: SIEM shows increased KMS timeout errors from 09:08-09:15Z, and proxy restart at 09:10Z. no signs of unauthorized decryption requests. collection saved to s3://forensic/INC-2026-0423/
lex: reverted PR #4782 and opened follow-up PR to add stronger auth to keystore sidecar, plus unit test to ensure no cache pop on decrypt failures. PR #4798.
morgan: good. we've kept the instance live with netpol + cache purge + rotation. are we comfortable marking severity down if no evidence of exfil?
ara: hold severity until we complete full postmortem and verify no cached keys left on any node or backup. also confirm KMS audit forwarding retention and HSM logs.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 status: containment=true, mitigation-in-progress. assigned severity=P3 pending postmortem.
sam: next steps (owners): rotate and validate keys @sam (30m), confirm netpol coverage @devon (15m), audit logs + upload @ara (45m), close PR followups @lex (60m), postmortem draft @morgan (EOD).
morgan: thanks all. I’ll draft the postmortem and add timeline + timeline artifacts to the incident thread. :thumbsup:
